findings.title: Checkout resolution is copied from `validate frontmatter`
findings.description: `resolveTemplatePath` repeats the project lookup in `validateFrontmatterAction` (validate.ts:154-166): `resolveProjectWorktree`, `store.getById`, the "Project not found" and "No projectPath configured" UserErrors, then `resolveOperationPath`. Other commands (build, plan, task, slice, arch, check, prompt) carry the same block too. The copy is not identical: validate.ts adds `?? project.projectPath`, which is redundant because `resolveOperationPath` already falls back to `projectPath` (worktree-overlay.ts:24). CLAUDE.md prohibits duplicated logic. Extract one helper in `utils/project.ts` and call it from both validate commands.

findings.title: `'slice-design'` is defined a second time
findings.description: `SLICE_DESIGN_DOC_TYPE = 'slice-design'` duplicates a value that already exists as the schema key and docType value in `FRONTMATTER_SCHEMAS` (frontmatterSchema.ts:74-76) and in `FILENAME_SEGMENT_TO_DOCTYPE` (frontmatterSchema.ts:148). CLAUDE.md requires a value used in comparisons to be defined once. Export one constant from `frontmatterSchema.ts`, reference it there, and import it here.

findings.title: The usage error bypasses the CLI error contract
findings.description: The no-files check throws `SliceDesignValidationError`. The same file uses `UserError` for its other two failures, and `ErrorCode` already defines `INVALID_ARGUMENT` for this case (utils/errors.ts:5; used at project.ts:416). Effects: in human mode the message gets an `Error:` prefix (errors.ts:66) instead of the clean UserError form, and in JSON mode `code` is `UNKNOWN` instead of `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Use `new UserError('no files given. Usage: cf validate design <file...>', 'INVALID_ARGUMENT')`.

findings.title: Several exports have no consumer
findings.description: `requiredHeadings`, `documentHeadingKeys`, `missingHeadings`, and their types are exported from the browser-safe entry point. `SLICE_DESIGN_DOC_TYPE` is exported from node.ts:34. A search of `packages/` finds no users outside core's own schema and tests. Each export is public API to maintain. Remove the unused ones, or document the consumer they are meant for.

findings.title: Read errors are misclassified
findings.description: `validateFile` calls `parseFrontmatter` before its own read. That parser catches every error and returns `{ data: {} }` (frontmatterParser.ts:63-65). A read failure there becomes a `doctype` FAIL with exit 1, not "cannot read file" with exit 2. Preflight's R_OK check makes this a narrow race. The file is also read twice (line 102). Separately, `loadRequiredHeadings` (lines 52-61) tells the user to run `cf guides update` for every template read error, including EACCES, which that command does not fix. The `cause` is attached, but `handleError` prints only `err.message`, so the error code never reaches the user. Read each file once, and include the underlying error code in the message.

findings.title: An empty required key silently passes any heading
findings.description: A required template heading whose key normalizes to empty matches any same-level document heading. For example, `## (optional)` yields text `''` (lines 36-40), and `doc.text.startsWith('')` is always true. Nothing reports it. The current template has no such heading, so this is latent. CLAUDE.md prohibits silent passes. Throw in `requiredHeadings` when a key is empty, or pin the behavior with a test.

findings.title: Heading and fence detection only accept column 0
findings.description: `HEADING_PATTERN` rejects the up-to-three-space indent CommonMark allows, and the fence check at line 63 rejects indented and `~~~` fences. This matches the bash script's column-0 rules, so it is a parity choice. CLAUDE.md asks for lenient parsing, though. A heading inside an indented fence in a list item is counted as a document heading, which can produce a false PASS. Accept leading whitespace and `~~~`, or record the limitation. Add a test that uses an indented fence.

findings.title: The native check and the guide script disagree on docType
findings.description: The native check accepts `docType: "slice-design"`, because `parseFrontmatter` strips quotes. The test "accepts a quoted docType" pins that. The guide script requires an exact unquoted line (`scripts/validate-slice-design:23,81-86`). The same file can pass `cf validate design` and fail the script. Choose one rule and make both follow it.

findings.title: Tests depend on live user documents
findings.description: `PASSING_DESIGNS` reads four slice documents from `project-documents/user/slices/`, and `sliceDesignFiles.test.ts:18-21` reads `214` the same way. The tests assert those files pass. Editing, archiving, or renaming one breaks the unit suite for an unrelated reason. Keep one real-world design, and copy the rest into `tests/fixtures/`. The `## Value`-removal regex is also duplicated between the CLI test (`brokenCopy`) and the core test (`withoutValueSection`). Move it into one shared fixture helper.

findings.title: New file names don't follow the TypeScript rule
findings.description: The three new source files use camelCase. The TypeScript rule in `.claude/rules/typescript.md` says kebab-case. The repo is mixed: `frontmatterFileValidator.ts` and `routedFixes.ts` are camelCase, while `setup-ide.ts` and `project-autoset.ts` are kebab-case. The new files match their neighbors, which is reasonable. Decide which convention the project wants and apply it consistently.

findings.title: The validator matches the guide script's semantics
findings.description: Read against the bash reference: the marker is the line after a heading. Keys are lowercased, with HTML comments, parentheticals, and `{placeholder}` suffixes removed. Matching is prefix-based at the same level. Fenced blocks are skipped. The docType failure message is identical. CRLF is handled. The four fixture designs declare `docType: slice-design` and contain the required headings the tests reference.

The usage error bypasses the CLI error contract
